#### 1. renal tubular acidosis, distal, 2, with progressive sensorineural hearing loss  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.494)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1222556, Reactome:R-HSA-77387, Reactome:R-HSA-917977, Reactome:R-HSA-9639288)

**Proposed mechanism:** TCIRG1 (HGNC:11787) —BINDS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005925); ATP6V1B1 (HGNC:910) —BINDS→ V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005925); V-ATPase assembly and function (GO:0005925) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal acidification (GO:0000314); TCIRG1 (HGNC:11787) —DISRUPTS→ Osteopetrosis (HP:0004260); ATP6V1B1 (HGNC:910) —DISRUPTS→ Renal tubular acidosis (HP:0001801); ATP6V1B1 (HGNC:910) —DISRUPTS→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405). Loss-of-function mutations in TCIRG1 (osteopetrosis) and ATP6V1B1 (renal tubular acidosis, hearing loss) disrupt the assembly and function of the V-ATPase proton pump, leading to impaired lysosomal acidification. This impaired acidification has distinct downstream consequences, manifesting as osteopetrosis in bone due to defective osteoclast resorption, and renal tubular acidosis due to impaired proton secretion in the kidney, and sensorineural hearing loss in the cochlea.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in TCIRG1 in patients with distal renal tubular acidosis and progressive sensorineural hearing loss, or identification of a pathogenic variant in ATP6V1B1 in patients with osteopetrosis, without involvement of the other gene. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common pathogenic variant (allele frequency > 1%) in either TCIRG1 or ATP6V1B1 that perfectly segregates with both disease phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of V-ATPase in these distinct diseases opens avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting proton pump activity or lysosomal function, potentially benefiting patients with both osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis with hearing loss, or related conditions involving V-ATPase dysfunction.
